intro: Printable quick references for AZ-104: CLI and PowerShell, identity, storage, compute, networking, monitoring.

sheets.title: CLI and PowerShell
sheets.blurb: The Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell commands used most often in labs and on the exam.

blocks.title: Azure CLI essentials
rows: Sign in and pick a subscription
Delete a group and everything in it
az vm create -g rg1 -n vm1 --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_B2s --admin-username azureuser --generate-ssh-keys
List VMs (output: json, table, tsv, yaml)
az vm start | stop | deallocate | restart -g rg1 -n vm1
Power state (stopped still bills compute; deallocate does not)
az vm resize -g rg1 -n vm1 --size Standard_D2s_v5
az network vnet create -g rg1 -n vnet1 --address-prefixes 10.0.0.0/16 --subnet-name s1 --subnet-prefixes 10.0.1.0/24
az network nsg rule create -g rg1 --nsg-name nsg1 -n allow-https --priority 200 --access Allow --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 443
az network vnet peering create -g rg1 -n a-to-b --vnet-name vnetA --remote-vnet vnetB --allow-vnet-access
az storage account create -n <name> -g rg1 --sku Standard_LRS --kind StorageV2
Storage account (3-24 lowercase letters or digits, globally unique)
az storage container create --account-name <n> -n data --auth-mode login
az storage blob upload --account-name <n> -c data -f file.txt -n file.txt --auth-mode login
az ad user create  /  az ad group member add
az webapp create -g rg1 -p plan1 -n app1 --runtime "NODE:20-lts"
az webapp deployment slot create -g rg1 -n app1 --slot staging
az deployment group create -g rg1 --template-file main.bicep
Deploy a Bicep or ARM template

sheets.title: Identity and governance
sheets.blurb: RBAC roles, Entra ID, policy, locks and management groups.

blocks.title: Azure RBAC built-in roles
head: Role
Can
rows: Create and manage resources; cannot assign roles
Manage access to resources (assign roles), nothing else
Manage VMs, not the network or storage they use
Storage Blob Data Reader / Contributor / Owner
Data-plane access to blobs (separate from management roles)

blocks.title: Identity and access facts
items: Scope hierarchy: management group > subscription > resource group > resource. Assignments inherit downward; deny assignments and Azure Policy can restrict further.

Azure RBAC (resources) is separate from Microsoft Entra roles (the directory: Global Administrator, User Administrator...). A Global Administrator can elevate to User Access Administrator at root scope.
Custom roles: JSON with Actions, NotActions, DataActions, AssignableScopes. Role assignment = security principal + role + scope.
Entra user types: member and guest (B2B). Groups: Security and Microsoft 365; membership Assigned, Dynamic User or Dynamic Device (Entra ID P1+).
Licenses: Free, P1 (dynamic groups, conditional access, SSPR writeback), P2 (PIM, Identity Protection). Devices: Registered, Joined, Hybrid joined.

SSPR: users register authentication methods and reset their own password; writing the new password back to on-premises AD needs P1 or higher. MFA is enforced per user, by security defaults or by Conditional Access.
Managed identities: system-assigned (tied to the resource lifecycle) and user-assigned (shared). Use them instead of stored secrets.

blocks.title: Governance
head: Tool
What it does
rows: Evaluates resources against rules. Effects: Deny, Audit, Append, Modify, DeployIfNotExists, AuditIfNotExists, Disabled. Initiative = a group of policies
CanNotDelete (delete blocked) or ReadOnly (no changes). Apply at subscription, resource group or resource; they override RBAC
Name/value metadata for cost and ownership; not inherited by default (use Policy to enforce or inherit)
Up to 6 levels below the tenant root group; apply policy and RBAC across subscriptions
Budgets, alerts, cost analysis, advisor recommendations. Reservations and savings plans lower compute cost
A subscription must register a provider (Microsoft.Compute) before using it

blocks.title: Storage redundancy
head: Option
Copies / durability
Protects against
rows: LRS here + LRS in paired region (16 nines)
GRS plus read access to the secondary
ZRS in primary + LRS in secondary

blocks.title: Storage facts
items: Account kinds: StorageV2 (general purpose v2, default), BlockBlobStorage and FileStorage (premium). Services: Blob, Files, Queue, Table, Data Lake Gen2 (hierarchical namespace).
Blob tiers: Hot, Cool (30-day minimum), Cold (90 days), Archive (180 days, offline: rehydrate takes hours). Lifecycle management rules move or delete blobs automatically.
Access: account keys (full access, rotate), SAS (service, account, user-delegation; stored access policy can revoke), Entra ID RBAC (preferred), anonymous (container-level, can be disabled).

Security: firewalls and virtual networks, private endpoints, encryption at rest by default (Microsoft-managed or customer-managed keys), secure transfer required, soft delete, versioning, immutability (WORM).
Azure Files: SMB 445 / NFS shares; Azure File Sync caches shares on Windows Server. Tools: AzCopy, Storage Explorer, Azure Import/Export, Data Box.
Replication between accounts: object replication (blob). Failover: customer-managed account failover for GRS/GZRS.

sheets.title: Compute
sheets.blurb: VMs, scale sets, App Service, containers, templates, backup.

blocks.title: Compute choices
head: Service
Use it for
rows: Full OS control. Sizes: B burstable, D general, E memory, F compute, L storage, N GPU, M very large memory
Identical VMs that autoscale on metrics or schedule (uniform or flexible orchestration)
Web apps, APIs. Plans: Free/Shared (no custom TLS), Basic (custom domains, TLS), Standard+ (autoscale, slots), Premium, Isolated
Quick single containers, no orchestration (billed per second)
Managed Kubernetes; node pools, cluster autoscaler
Event-driven code; Consumption plan scales to zero

blocks.title: VM facts
items: Availability: single VM with Premium SSD 99.9%, availability set 99.95% (fault and update domains), availability zones 99.99%. Region pairs help disaster recovery.
Disks: Standard HDD, Standard SSD, Premium SSD (v1/v2), Ultra. Managed disks. Encryption: SSE by default, Azure Disk Encryption (BitLocker or dm-crypt), encryption at host.
Stopped (OS shutdown) still bills compute; stopped (deallocated) does not. Resizing may need a deallocate; reserved private IP stays, a dynamic public IP can change.
Moving a resource to another resource group or subscription changes its resource ID, and not every resource type supports a move. A region move uses Azure Resource Mover or a redeploy.
ARM templates (JSON) and Bicep are declarative infrastructure as code; deployment modes: Incremental (default) and Complete (deletes resources not in the template).
App Service slots swap content and settings; slot-specific (sticky) settings stay. Autoscale: rules on metrics or schedule with min, max and default instance counts.
Azure Backup for VMs uses a Recovery Services vault and a backup policy (daily, retention); Site Recovery replicates VMs to another region.

sheets.title: Networking
sheets.blurb: VNets, NSGs, peering, endpoints, gateways and load balancing.

blocks.title: Networking building blocks
head: Item
Key facts
rows: Address space CIDR, no overlap if you peer or connect. Azure reserves 5 addresses per subnet (first 4 and last)
Connects VNets over the Microsoft backbone; not transitive; global peering across regions. Create it in both directions
Stateful allow/deny by 5-tuple, priority 100-4096 (low number wins). Defaults: AllowVNetInBound, AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound, DenyAllInBound (65000-65500). Attach to a subnet and/or NIC
Group NICs so NSG rules refer to roles, not IPs
Override system routes (for example force traffic to a firewall, next hop type Virtual appliance)
Endpoint: subnet identity reaches a service's public endpoint over the backbone. Private Endpoint: a private IP in your VNet for one resource (Private Link) and DNS via a private zone
Basic (retiring) and Standard (static, zone-redundant, secure by default: needs an NSG to allow traffic)
Public zones for internet names; private zones resolve names inside linked VNets (auto-registration option)
RDP/SSH to VMs over TLS from the portal; no public IP on the VM (AzureBastionSubnet, at least /26)
Site-to-site, point-to-site and VNet-to-VNet encrypted tunnels over the internet (GatewaySubnet)
Private circuit from your network to Microsoft; not over the internet; connectivity provider
Managed stateful firewall; network and application rules, FQDN filtering, threat intelligence

blocks.title: Load balancing options
head: Service
Layer
Scope
Use
rows: Internal or public, health probes, zone-redundant
Edge acceleration, global failover, WAF, CDN-style caching
DNS-based routing: priority, weighted, performance, geographic, multivalue, subnet

sheets.title: Monitor and recover
sheets.blurb: Azure Monitor, alerts, Network Watcher, backup and Site Recovery.

blocks.title: Monitoring and recovery
head: Tool
Purpose
rows: Platform for metrics (numeric, near-real-time) and logs
Stores logs; query with Kusto Query Language (KQL)
Rule (signal, condition) triggers an action group (email, SMS, webhook, runbook, function). Types: metric, log, activity log
Subscription-level control-plane events (who did what, when); 90 days by default
Send resource logs and metrics to a workspace, storage or Event Hub
Application performance monitoring and availability tests
Guest OS metrics and logs; Data Collection Rules
Azure incidents / health of your resources
IP flow verify, next hop, connection troubleshoot, NSG flow logs, packet capture, topology
Recommendations for reliability, security, cost, performance, operational excellence
Azure Backup (VMs, SQL in VM, Files) and Site Recovery; soft delete protects deleted backups for 14 days
Newer vault type for disks, blobs and PostgreSQL
